source.title: When Machine Unlearning Meets Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Keep Secret or Forget Knowledge?
source.authors: Shang Wang; Tian-Qing Zhu; Da-Yong Ye; Wan-Lei Zhou

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure labels are garbled, and Table VIII is flattened so its before/after values cannot be reliably assigned.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether prompt rephrasing and attacks undo unlearning, using USR and other measures rather than the original studies’ methods. It also tests a RAG-based counter-method against these attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports prompt-rephrasing results for gradient ascent, in-context unlearning, µ-unlearning, and RAG-based unlearning; it also reports jailbreak, prompt-injection, and adaptive-injection results for RAG. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning after unlearning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. The table values for general-ability benchmarks are not extracted because their flattened layout does not reliably map values to rows.
record.test_reason: The study re-queries gradient ascent, in-context and µ-unlearning baselines with semantics-preserving rephrased prompts and measures how often they still forget (USR). This bears on A and E. It also proposes a RAG guardrail as a counter-method and attacks it with rephrasing, in-the-wild jailbreaks, prompt injection and adaptive override prompts, which bears on F. There is no fine-tuning, activation-ablation or quantization attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that RAG-based behavioral unlearning meets five criteria (effectiveness, universality, harmlessness, simplicity, robustness) and outperforms gradient ascent, in-context and µ-unlearning. They argue the baselines fail on rephrased prompts. They concede the LLM still retains the target knowledge and that adaptive prompts with enough leaked unlearned knowledge bypass the scheme, though they call this unlikely in practice.
record.recipe_differences: The paper's method modifies an external RAG knowledge base and prompt context rather than editing model weights. It evaluates gradient ascent, in-context unlearning, and µ-unlearning as baselines; it does not report testing Who's Harry Potter? or RMU.
record.method_sensitivity: Rephrasing changes USR for several baseline methods; adaptive-attack USR decreases as the exposed portion of unlearned knowledge grows. RAG retrieval quality is also discussed as affecting effectiveness.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
record.problems: Rephrasing outcomes are reported using USR, a judge-based forgetting measure, rather than direct recovered-knowledge accuracy. The paper does not compare attack recovery with a model that never learned the target. Table VIII is flattened and its before/after benchmark values cannot be assigned reliably. The standard jailbreak figure does not provide legible exact values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Table IV ROUGE values were omitted because the extracted rows already include USR and residual-memorization TPR, the more direct measures for the versions tested. Exact standard-attack figure values were not recoverable; the figure-only outcomes are represented with the accompanying textual descriptions in r33-r36. Table VIII numerical entries were not mapped because the flattened layout is ambiguous.

untested.parts: WMDP/Harry-Potter-style benchmarks, comparison against a never-trained model, and recovery by fine-tuning, quantization or internal edits. Baseline utility values are unreadable.
Entirely: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Entirely: no activation ablation or internal analysis. Authors only assert the RAG method leaves knowledge in the model.
Other languages, in-context information and jailbreaks against weight-based methods. Rephrasing on closed models is uninformative because in-context unlearning never worked there.
Resistance to fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization or direct access to the base model; the threat model excludes bypassing the RAG pipeline.

missing.what: Harmful-topic unlearning on fine-tuned Llama-2-7b-chat (91.2% harmful output before unlearning). HOP / USR: GA 45.8% / 29.6%, in-context 74.1% / 7.9%, µ 40.2% / 39.4%, RAG 1.0% / 99.3%.
RAG universality USR on GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.0, Llama-2-13b-chat, Vicuna-7B and PaLM 2 (96.4–100%).
Closed-model Min-K TPR: in-context 3.6% / 2.9% and RAG 1.5% / 1.3% on GPT-4o / Gemini. It is unclear how token log-likelihoods were obtained for closed models.
MMLU/ARC before and after unlearning for each method and target. The flattened table has 9 of 16 MMLU cells, so baseline utility cannot be assigned.
Retriever dependence: Self-RAG 98.2% and Contriever 97.6% retrieval accuracy versus GPT-4o 100%; misses occur on prompts without concept words.

record.verdict_notes: The RAG method is a context-injected refusal guardrail, not weight unlearning; the authors state knowledge stays in the model. Its rows were moved from A to F. USR is a GPT-4o judge comparing outputs before and after unlearning. Table VI's RAG Llama value (97.1%) conflicts with the text's '>97.4%', and Table XII's minimum (20.2%) with the text's '20.9%'. Min-K TPR on the closed models is methodologically unclear. Rows r1-r6 and r9-r14 are confirmed as recorded (A, partial).

versions.untested_parts: It evaluates target forgetting and general-ability benchmarks, and evaluates prompt robustness, but does not establish the full claim for every unlearning method or compare attack recovery against a model that never learned the target.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or small-set relearning attack is evaluated.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-edit analysis of whether knowledge was deleted versus inaccessible is performed.
No low-bit quantization attack is evaluated.
Tests semantic prompt rephrasing and, for RAG, jailbreak and prompt-injection attacks. It does not test other languages or in-context provision of target information.
Tests the RAG method against rephrasing, specified jailbreaks, prompt injection, and adaptive prompt injection. Does not test resistance to fine-tuning, internal edits, or quantization.
